In summary, our research is concerned with

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
renin secretion is a function of both renal and extrarenal factors, and the system configuration indicates the relative importance of these factors in different physiologic conditions.
the control system for the renin secretion rate is a parallel configuration with independent receptor functions.

the renin-aldosterone axis is a highly sensitive and effective system which can respond to changes in sodium intake and extracellular volume, but that the system is also capable of responding to a variety of stimuli which may or may not be associated with changes in sodium intake or extracellular fluid volume.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a low sodium diet and a nonhypotensive blood loss are two examples of conditions which produce increased renin secretion through the renal vascular receptor.
the renin-aldosterone response to a change in blood volume is a complex function of both the magnitude of the change and the time course of its onset.
the renin-aldosterone response to a low-sodium diet is a function of the renal receptors, whereas the response to hemorrhage is a function of both the renal and the baroreceptor mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the renin-aldosterone-angiotensins system has a complex control system that can be analyzed using control theory.
